subject: SLA safety anchor for AeroMed progressive rollout - request and ask
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Peter Salmon <peter.salmon@aeromed-health.com>
Cc: AeroMed Platform Team <platform@aeromed-health.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: SLA safety anchor for AeroMed progressive rollout - request and ask

Hi all,

AeroMed is planning a progressive launch of their clinical notes summarization feature next week. Legal and CS have agreed to the commercial terms, but they asked for a short SLA safety anchor to reduce risk during the first 72 hours of live traffic.

In plain terms they want: a) an automatic, service-level fallback if tail latency or error-rate crosses a gate, and b) the ability to temporarily pin traffic to a V2 variant we know is stable while we remediate. They also want visibility into how that fallback affects their credit/eventing.

Ask: can Eng and Product sign off on an exception that adds a temporary "safety anchor" to the standard rollout policy for this account? Proposed parameters below — please respond with feasibility and any tweaks by EOD tomorrow so CS can confirm with AeroMed.

Proposed safety anchor (draft):
- Canary window: 72h with 5% initial traffic, step to 30% at 24h if gates pass.
- Gate thresholds: 95th latency increase > 200ms over baseline OR error-rate > 1.0% sustained for 5m triggers fallback.
- Fallback behavior: immediate split-route overflow to the pinned v2-stable model variant and route remaining traffic to a lower-cost, higher-latency variant when capacity constrained.
- Auto-pin timeout: 48h after fallback; requires manual engineer approval to unpin earlier.
- Observability: per-route token-level latency, pre/post-fallback sample logs, and an hourly digest sent to AeroMed and CS.

Attachments: routing_playbook.pdf (draft), canary-config.yaml (example), sla-delta-summary.xlsx (commercial impact).

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
From: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Peter Salmon <peter.salmon@aeromed-health.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 17:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA safety anchor for AeroMed progressive rollout - request and ask

Thanks Sean — quick read and a few clarifying notes from Product:

1) Feasible: we can support a 72h window with the gate thresholds you listed. Marcus — the 1.0% error-rate gating is fine as long as we use 5m sustained windows and exclude client-side 429/limit-induced errors.

2) Pin semantics: product prefers an explicit "anchor" state rather than a hard pin. Anchor = route traffic to v2-stable by default while keeping canary telemetry open. That lets us collect fidelity metrics while minimizing change surface. We should keep manual unpin as the default action to ensure CS is in the loop.

3) Auto-unpin policy: recommend auto-unpin be disabled for this initial exception — manual unpin only. If AeroMed requests auto-unpin later we can revisit after two juice cycles of telemetry.

4) Acceptance criteria for step-up at 24h: must have 95th latency within 120ms of baseline, error-rate <0.5% and no more than 1 regression in model quality evals on our smoke prompts.

I'll coordinate with Marcus to produce a concrete config and the observability playbook. If everyone agrees I'll communicate this as the exception language to AeroMed and get written acknowledgement.

- Grace

--
Grace Oconnor
Director, Product Management, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA safety anchor for AeroMed progressive rollout - request and ask

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of items from AeroMed:

- We agree with the anchor approach and prefer manual unpin.
- Can you confirm the credit/compensation model if a fallback is triggered? Specifically, how will an SLA credit be calculated for a routed fallback period vs a total outage?
- We also want a short post-mortem timeline commitment (72h) if a fallback happens.

If you can confirm the compensation calc and the PM timeline we'll sign off on the exception and proceed with the pilot next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Peter

--
Peter Salmon
Head of Platform, AeroMed Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Peter Salmon <peter.salmon@aeromed-health.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA safety anchor for AeroMed progressive rollout - request and ask

Quick technical confirmation and playbook summary:

- Feasibility: fully supported. We will implement an "anchor" routing state via a canary policy that sets routing weights and an explicit pin flag. The routing controller will accept a fallback webhook trigger when pre-configured telemetry gates are breached.

- Gate implementation: use a rolling 5m window with the alerted aggregation at 1m resolution. Gate detection is based on service-internal 95th p95 latency and backend 5xx/error percent (server-side only). We will ignore client throttling (429) and malformed requests in the gate calc.

- Fallback action: upon gate trip the controller will: 1) move 100% new sessions to v2-stable for a soft-anchor duration; 2) mark the canary as "quarantined" and emit a high-priority incident to our ops channel; 3) spawn an automated diagnostic job to collect token-level traces and KV cache heatmaps; 4) persist the route state in the audit log for compliance.

- Pin/unpin workflow: unpin requires a two-person approval (Engineering + CS) documented in the Jira ticket INF-1872. Auto-unpin will be disabled for this exception.

- Rollback SLA credit model (proposal): we propose prorated credit based on time-in-fallback where the fallback caused a measurable latency delta > 150ms on 95th. Example calc: credit = min(5% monthly usage, usage * (delta_ms / baseline_ms) * weighting). I'll attach a worked example in sla-delta-summary.xlsx.

Attachments: canary-config.yaml (actual config we plan to push), routing_playbook.pdf (ops steps).

I'll ship the canary config to staging and ping the AeroMed team for an on-call dry-run.

Marcus
